_doc: Source ledger for chokepoint / headline shares. Each entry ties a figure to a NAMED source AND the quoted table row / sentence, so a bare citation cannot hide a misread. Rule: a chokepoint tagged conf=measured MUST have an entry here whose quoted row supports its share; if the source has no computable figure, the tag is estimate/attributed. check.py enforces presence (check_ledger).
_method: USGS MCS PDFs fetched with a browser User-Agent (the default fetch UA gets 403); extracted with `pdftotext -raw` (with -layout the reserves column drifts onto the wrong country row). Shares computed from the 2024 production/reserves column.

phosphate-food.quoted_row: Morocco 33,000 30,000 50,000,000 | World total (rounded) 233,000 240,000 74,000,000 (cols: 2023 prod, 2024 prod, reserves)

pgm-catalyst.claim: South Africa ~78% of world PGM reserves (platinum ~71%; palladium Russia-led)
pgm-catalyst.quoted_row: South Africa ... 125,000 120,000 63,000,000 | World total ... 179,000 170,000 >81,000,000; 'resources and reserves are in the Bushveld Complex in South Africa'

steel-alloys.claim: Brazil ~92% of world niobium production (chokepoint); vanadium China ~70% (stat)
steel-alloys.source: USGS MCS 2025 — Niobium; USGS MCS 2025 — Vanadium
steel-alloys.quoted_row: Niobium: 'Brazil ... approximately 92% of global production, followed by Canada with about 7%.' | Vanadium: China e70,000 70,000 4,100 | World total 104,000 100,000 18,000
steel-alloys.computed: niobium 92% verbatim; vanadium 70,000/100,000 = 70% (was ~64% in atlas -> corrected)

boron.claim: Turkey ~73% of world borate reserves (Eti Maden company estimate)
boron.source: USGS MCS 2025 — Boron (no world total); Eti Maden (company claim)
boron.quoted_row: 'World total4 XX XX XX' + footnote 4: 'World totals cannot be calculated because production and reserves are not reported in a consistent manner by all countries.' The '~70%' had been misread from 'About 70% of all deposits in Turkey are colemanite' (deposit TYPE, not world share).
boron.computed: NO world reserves total exists in USGS -> a world % is not computable; ~73% is Eti Maden's own claim, hence estimate

tungsten.claim: China ~83% of world tungsten mine production

strontium.claim: Iran ~39% of world celestite production (tied with Spain)
strontium.computed: Iran 200,000/510,000 = 39% (Spain also 200,000 = 39%; China 80,000 = 16%) -> was 'Iran ~58%' in atlas -> corrected

gallium.claim: China ~98% of world primary (low-purity) gallium production
gallium.quoted_row: 'China accounted for 99% of worldwide primary low-purity gallium production.'
gallium.computed: USGS says 99%; atlas ~98% is within rounding

bismuth.quoted_row: China 13,300 13,000 NA | World total (rounded) 16,200 16,000 NA; 'China, the leading producer and exporter'

germanium.quoted_row: 'China continued to be the leading global producer and exporter of germanium metal'; 'most producers do not publicly report germanium' output.
germanium.computed: USGS publishes NO country production table for germanium -> ~60% is an industry estimate, not measurable; retagged estimate

antimony.claim: China refining chokepoint (mine ~60%; refining/oxide dominance is the binding stage)
antimony.quoted_row: China e62,300 60,000 670,000 | World total (rounded) 106,000 100,000 >2,000,000; US import 'Oxide: China 76%'
antimony.computed: mine 60,000/100,000 = 60%; chokepoint is refining/oxide + Sep-2024 export controls, not the mine share
